verses.zh: 这是耶和华在摩押地吩咐摩西与以色列人立约的话，是在他和他们于何烈山所立的约之外。
verses.en: (28:69)[NOTE:1] These are the words of the covenant that the Lord commanded Moses to make with the people of Israel in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant he had made with them at Horeb.[NOTE:2]
notes: Beginning with 29:1, the verse numbers through 29:29 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 29:1 ET = 28:69 HT, 29:2 ET = 29:1 HT, 29:3 ET = 29:2 HT, etc., through 29:29 ET = 29:28 HT. With 30:1 the verse numbers in the ET and HT are again the same.
Horeb is another name for Mount Sinai (which some English versions substitute here for clarity, cf. NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 摩西召了以色列众人来，对他们说：「耶和华在埃及地，在你们眼前向法老和他众臣仆，并他全地所行的一切事，你们都看见了，
verses.en: Moses proclaimed to all Israel as follows: “You have seen all that the Lord did[NOTE:1] in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, all his servants, and his land.
notes: The Hebrew text includes “to your eyes,” but this is redundant in English style (cf. the preceding “you have seen”) and is omitted in the translation.

verses.zh: 就是你亲眼看见的大试验和神迹，并那些大奇事。
verses.en: Your eyes have seen the great judgments,[NOTE:1] those signs and mighty wonders.
notes: Heb “testings.” This is a reference to the plagues; see note at 4:34.

verses.zh: 但耶和华到今日没有使你们心能明白，眼能看见，耳能听见。
verses.en: But to this very day the Lord has not given you an understanding mind, perceptive eyes, or discerning ears![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “a heart to know, eyes to see and ears to hear” (NASB similar); NAB, NRSV “a mind to understand, or eyes to see, or ears to hear.”

verses.zh: 我领你们在旷野四十年，你们身上的衣服并没有穿破，脚上的鞋也没有穿坏。
verses.en: I have led you through the wilderness for 40 years. Your clothing has not worn out[NOTE:1] nor have your sandals[NOTE:2] deteriorated.
notes: The Hebrew text includes “on you.” This has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
The Hebrew text includes “from on your feet.”

verses.zh: 你们没有吃饼，也没有喝清酒浓酒。这要使你们知道，耶和华是你们的　神。
verses.en: You have eaten no bread and drunk no wine or beer—all so that you might know that I[NOTE:1] am the Lord your God!
notes: The LXX reads “that he is the Lord your God.”

verses.zh: 你们来到这地方，希实本王西宏、巴珊王噩都出来与我们交战，我们就击杀了他们，
verses.en: When you came to this place King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan came out to make war and we defeated them.

verses.zh: 取了他们的地给流便支派、迦得支派，和玛拿西半支派为业。
verses.en: Then we took their land and gave it as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

verses.zh: 所以你们要谨守遵行这约的话，好叫你们在一切所行的事上亨通。
verses.en: “Therefore, keep the terms[NOTE:1] of this covenant and obey them so that you may be successful in everything you do.
notes: Heb “words.”

verses.zh: 「今日，你们的首领、族长（原文是支派）、长老、官长、以色列的男丁，你们的妻子儿女，和营中寄居的，以及为你们劈柴挑水的人，都站在耶和华―你们的　神面前，
verses.en: You are standing today, all of you, before the Lord your God—the heads of your tribes,[NOTE:1] your elders, your officials, every Israelite man,
notes: Heb “your heads, your tribes.” The Syriac presupposes either “heads of your tribes” or “your heads, your judges,” etc. (reading שֹׁפְטֵכֶם [shofetekhem] for שִׁבְטֵיכֶם [shivtekhem]). Its comparative difficulty favors the originality of the MT reading. Cf. KJV “your captains of your tribes”; NRSV “the leaders of your tribes”; NLT “your tribal leaders.”

verses.zh: a
verses.en: your infants, your wives, and the[NOTE:1] resident foreigners[NOTE:2] living in your encampment, those who chop wood and those who carry water—
notes: Heb “your.”

The ger (גֵּר) “foreign resident” here enters into the covenant with the community if Israel. Elsewhere in Mosaic Law the ger make sacrifices to the Lord (Lev 17:8; 22:18; Num 15:14) and participate in Israel’s religious festivals: Passover Exod 12:48; Day of Atonement Lev 16:29; Feast of Weeks Deut 16:10-14; Feast of Tabernacles/Temporary Shelters Deut 31:12. Several passages emphasize equal standing under Mosaic Law (Exod 12:49; Lev 24:22; Num 9:14; 15:15, 16, 26, 29; 19:10; 35:15; Deut 1:16 or similar obligations Exod 20:10; 23:12; Lev 16:29; 17:10, 12, 13; 18:26; 24:16; Num 15:14. In many respects these ger (גֵּר) appear to be naturalized citizens who could not own land (land was allotted by tribe).

verses.zh: 为要你顺从耶和华―你　神今日与你所立的约，向你所起的誓。
verses.en: so that you may enter by oath into the covenant the Lord your God is making with you today.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for you to pass on into the covenant of the Lord your God and into his oath, which the Lord your God is cutting with you today.”

verses.zh: 这样，他要照他向你所应许的话，又向你列祖亚伯拉罕、以撒、雅各所起的誓，今日立你作他的子民，他作你的　神。
verses.en: Today he will affirm that you are his people and that he is your God,[NOTE:1] just as he promised you and as he swore by oath to your ancestors[NOTE:2] Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
notes: Heb “in order to establish you today to him for a people and he will be to you for God.” Verses 10-13 are one long sentence in Hebrew. The translation divides this into two sentences for stylistic reasons.
Heb “fathers” (also in v. 25).

verses.zh: 我不但与你们立这约，起这誓，
verses.en: It is not with you alone that I am making this covenant by oath,

verses.zh: 凡与我们一同站在耶和华―我们　神面前的，并今日不在我们这里的人，我也与他们立这约，起这誓。
verses.en: but with whoever stands with us here today before the Lord our God as well as those not with us here today.[NOTE:1]
notes: This is interpreted by some English versions as a reference to generations not yet born (cf. TEV, CEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 「我们曾住过埃及地，也从列国经过；这是你们知道的。
verses.en: “(For you know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we crossed through the nations as we traveled.

verses.zh: 你们也看见他们中间可憎之物，并他们木、石、金、银的偶像。
verses.en: You have seen their detestable things[NOTE:1] and idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold.)[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew term שִׁקּוּץ (shiqquts) refers to anything out of keeping with the nature and character of Yahweh and therefore to be avoided by his people Israel. It is commonly used with or as a synonym for תּוֹעֵבָה (toʿevah, “detestable, abhorrent”; 2 Kgs 23:13; Jer 16:18; Ezek 5:11; 7:20; 11:18, 21; see note on the term “abhorrent” in Deut 7:25). See M. Grisanti, NIDOTTE 4:243-46.
The Hebrew text includes “which were with them.” Verses 16-17 constitute a parenthetical comment.

verses.zh: 惟恐你们中间，或男或女，或族长或支派长，今日心里偏离耶和华―我们的　神，去事奉那些国的　神；又怕你们中间有恶根生出苦菜和茵蔯来，
verses.en: Beware that the heart of no man, woman, clan, or tribe among you turns away from the Lord our God today to pursue and serve the gods of those nations; beware that there is among you no root producing poisonous and bitter fruit.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “yielding fruit poisonous and wormwood.” The Hebrew noun לַעֲנָה (laʿanah) literally means “wormwood” (so KJV, ASV, NAB, NASB), but is used figuratively for anything extremely bitter, thus here “fruit poisonous and bitter.”

verses.zh: 听见这咒诅的话，心里仍是自夸说：『我虽然行事心里顽梗，连累众人，却还是平安。』
verses.en: When such a person[NOTE:1] hears the words of this oath he secretly[NOTE:2] blesses himself[NOTE:3] and says, ‘I will have peace though I continue to walk with a stubborn spirit.’[NOTE:4] This will destroy[NOTE:5] the watered ground with the parched.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the subject of the warning in v. 18) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “in his heart.”
Or “invokes a blessing on himself.” A formalized word of blessing is in view, the content of which appears later in the verse.
Heb “heart.”
Heb “thus destroying.” For stylistic reasons the translation begins a new sentence here.

Heb “the watered with the parched.” The word “ground” is implied. The exact meaning of the phrase is uncertain although it appears to be figurative. This appears to be a proverbial observation employing a figure of speech (a merism) suggesting totality. That is, the Israelite who violates the letter and even spirit of the covenant will harm not only himself but everything he touches—“the watered and the parched.” Cf. CEV “you will cause the rest of Israel to be punished along with you.”

verses.zh: 耶和华必不饶恕他；耶和华的怒气与愤恨要向他发作，如烟冒出，将这书上所写的一切咒诅都加在他身上。耶和华又要从天下涂抹他的名，
verses.en: The Lord will be unwilling to forgive him, and his intense anger[NOTE:1] will rage[NOTE:2] against that man; all the curses[NOTE:3] written in this scroll will fall upon him,[NOTE:4] and the Lord will obliterate his name from memory.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “the wrath of the Lord and his zeal.” The expression is a hendiadys, a figure in which the second noun becomes adjectival to the first.
Heb “smoke,” or “smolder.”
Heb “the entire oath.”
Or “will lie in wait against him.”
Heb “blot out his name from under the sky.”

verses.zh: 也必照着写在律法书上、约中的一切咒诅将他从以色列众支派中分别出来，使他受祸。
verses.en: The Lord will single him out[NOTE:1] for judgment[NOTE:2] from all the tribes of Israel according to all the curses of the covenant written in this scroll of the law.
notes: Heb “set him apart.”
Heb “for evil”; NAB “for doom”; NASB “for adversity”; NIV “for disaster”; NRSV “for calamity.”

verses.zh: 你们的后代，就是以后兴起来的子孙，和远方来的外人，看见这地的灾殃，并耶和华所降与这地的疾病，
verses.en: The generation to come—your descendants who will rise up after you, as well as the foreigner who will come from distant places—will see[NOTE:1] the afflictions of that land and the illnesses that the Lord has brought on it.
notes: Heb “will say and see.” One expects a quotation to appear, but it seems to be omitted. To avoid confusion in the translation, the verb “will say” is omitted.

verses.zh: 又看见遍地有硫磺，有盐卤，有火迹，没有耕种，没有出产，连草都不生长―好像耶和华在忿怒中所倾覆的所多玛、蛾摩拉、押玛、洗扁一样―
verses.en: The whole land will be covered with brimstone, salt, and burning debris; it will not be planted nor will it sprout or produce grass. It will resemble the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboyim, which the Lord destroyed in his intense anger.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the anger and the wrath.” This construction is a hendiadys intended to intensify the emotion.

verses.zh: 所看见的人，连万国人，都必问说：『耶和华为何向此地这样行呢？这样大发烈怒是甚么意思呢？』
verses.en: Then all the nations will ask, ‘Why has the Lord done all this to this land? What is this fierce, heated display of anger[NOTE:1] all about?’
notes: Heb “this great burning of anger”; KJV “the heat of this great anger.”

verses.zh: 人必回答说：『是因这地的人离弃了耶和华―他们列祖的　神，领他们出埃及地的时候与他们所立的约，
verses.en: Then people will say, ‘Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord, the God of their ancestors, which he made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.

verses.zh: 去事奉敬拜素不认识的别神，是耶和华所未曾给他们安排的。
verses.en: They went and served other gods and worshiped them, gods they did not know and that he did not permit them to worship.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “did not assign to them”; NASB, NRSV “had not allotted to them.”

verses.zh: 所以耶和华的怒气向这地发作，将这书上所写的一切咒诅都降在这地上。
verses.en: That is why the Lord’s anger erupted against this land, bringing on it all the curses[NOTE:1] written in this scroll.
notes: Heb “the entire curse.”

verses.zh: 耶和华在怒气、忿怒、大恼恨中将他们从本地拔出来，扔在别的地上，像今日一样。』
verses.en: So the Lord has uprooted them from their land in anger, wrath, and great rage and has deported them to another land, as is clear today.’

verses.zh: 「隐秘的事是属耶和华―我们　神的；惟有明显的事是永远属我们和我们子孙的，好叫我们遵行这律法上的一切话。」
verses.en: The secret things belong to the Lord our God, but those that are revealed belong to us and our descendants[NOTE:1] forever, so that we might obey all the words of this law.
notes: Heb “sons” (so NASB); KJV, ASV, NIV, NRSV “children.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 29:1

1These are the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses to
make with the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant which He had made with them at Horeb.

29:1 "the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses" This is Moses' third
address in Deuteronomy (chapters 29-30). He reminds Israel that these laws are from YHWH, not himself. See outline of Moses'
sermons in Introduction to Deuteronomy, VIII.

▣ "besides the covenant" This refers to two covenants

- at Mt. Sinai/Horeb (Exodus 19-24)

- on the plains of Moab (cf. Deut. 1:5; 5:1,3,5-26). It was spelled out clearly in Exodus 20-31.

It was renewed in Exodus 34; Deuteronomy 29-30; and Joshua 24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 29:2-9

2And Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, "You have seen all that the Lord
did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh and all his servants and all his land; 3the great trials which your eyes have seen, those great signs and wonders.
4Yet to this day the Lord has not given you a heart to know, nor eyes to see, nor ears to hear. 5I have led you forty years
in the wilderness; your clothes have not worn out on you, and your sandal has not worn out on your foot. 6You have not eaten bread, nor have you drunk wine or strong
drink, in order that you might know that I am the Lord your God. 7When you reached this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon and Og the king
of Bashan came out to meet us for battle, but we defeated them; 8and we took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe
of the Manassites. 9So keep the words of this covenant to do them, that you may prosper in all that you do."

29:2 "all Israel" This usually refers to only the elders, but because of Deut. 29:1-13, it seems to refer to the entire nation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

29:2-3 "You have seen. . .your eyes have seen" This is a figure of speech (cf. Deut. 4:34; 7:19) because these people
were the children of those who had seen (cf. Num. 14:29; Deut. 5:2-4). Verses 2-8 form a historical review like chapters 1-4, which
was a common element of Near Eastern treaties.

▣ "sign and wonders" These terms "signs" (BDB 16) and "wonders" (BDB 68) are mentioned often in
Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:34; 6:22; 7:19; 11:3; 26:8; 28:46; 29:2; 34:11) to help the current generation of Israelis to remember YHWH's
powerful, gracious acts of deliverance and provisions (cf. Deut. 29:5-7) during the Exodus and Wilderness Wandering Period.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGN (OT)

29:4 "to this day" This recurrent phrase may denote a later editor. See full note at Deut. 3:14.

The blindness of Israel to their special place in YHWH's eternal redemptive plan was not
just an ancient problem (i.e. Deut. 29:4), but also a current problem (cf. Matt. 13:14-17; Mark 4:10-12; Luke 8:9-10;
John 12:36b-43; Acts 28:26-27; and especially Rom. 11:25-32).

The gospel is described as the predetermined plan and foreknowledge of God (cf. Acts 2:23;
also note 3:18; 4:28; 13:29).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREKNOWLEDGE

▣ "the Lord has not given you a heart to know, nor eyes to see, nor ears to hear" The
Israelites of the exodus and wilderness wanderings saw the physical, but did not comprehend the spiritual dimension of YHWH's
actions (i.e. they were a special covenant people who were part of an eternal redemptive plan). This phrase becomes imagery
for spiritual blindness and hardness (cf. Isa. 6:9-10; Acts 28:26-27; Rom. 11:8).

There is a word play between Deut. 29:2, "you have seen" and Deut. 29:4, where it is stated they
cannot see! This may refer to Israel's rebellions mentioned in Deut. 9:7-24. Without faith God is invisible in history, but
with faith history becomes God's track record. It takes a gift (i.e. "given," BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PERFECT) of
YHWH's grace for fallen humans to sense and understand His presence!

29:5 "clothes have not worn out. . .sandal has not worn out" The Jewish commentator, Rashi, says clothes and
shoes grew as the children grew (cf. Deut. 8:4; Neh. 9:21).

29:6 Verses 5 and 6 show God's providential care during the entire period of judgment known as the Wilderness
Wandering Period (cf. Num. 14:26-35; Deut. 8:2-3). The Israelites were to help maintain the relationship by focusing on YHWH
(not food, drink produced by human hands, but on His provision). But these verses also show the continual spiritual
blindness of YHWH's people (cf. Isa. 6:9-10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

29:7 This shows YHWH's military presence on behalf of Israel (cf. Num. 21:21-24, 33-35; and Deut. 2:26-3:17).

29:8 These are the tribes that settled on the eastern side of Jordan (cf. Deut. 3:12-13; Num. 32:28-32).

29:9 "So keep the words. . .do them" The conditional nature of the covenant (i.e. "keep," BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal
PERFECT with waw and "do," BDB 793, KB 889, Qal PERFECT with waw)
is recurrent in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:2,6,9,15,23,40; 5:1,10,12,29,32; 6:2,3,12,17,25; 7:9,11,12;
8:1,2,6,11; 10:13; 11:1,8,16,22,32; 12:1,28,32; 15:5; 16:12; 17:19; 19:9;
24:8; 26:16,17,18; 27:1; 28:1,9,13,15,45,58; 29:9; 30:10,16; 31:12; 32:46).
Obedience is a visible measure of the spiritual faithfulness of Israel. To love YHWH is to obey YHWH!

This verse was later read by the rabbis when some of the people were publicly whipped (cf. Deut. 25:3). It
contains 13 words to correspond to 13 stripes. Psalm 78:38 was also read.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "that you may prosper in all that you do" This VERB (BDB 968, KB 1328, Hiphil
IMPERFECT) usually means "be prudent" or "circumspect," but in the Hiphil stem it can mean
"prosper," "have success" (cf. Josh. 1:7-8; 1 Sam. 18:5,14,15; 1 Kgs. 2:3; 2 Kgs. 18:7; 1 Chr. 22:13). Notice that success
and prosperity are contingent on obedience!

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 29:10-13

10"You stand today, all of you, before the Lord your God:
your chiefs, your tribes, your elders and your officers, even all the men of Israel, 11your little ones, your wives, and the alien who is within
your camps, from the one who chops your wood to the one who draws your water, 12that you may enter into the covenant with the
Lord your God, and into His oath which the Lord your God is making with you today, 13in order that He may
establish you today as His people and that He may be your God, just as He spoke to you and as He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

29:10 "You stand" Notice the different groupings of Israeli society mentioned in Deut. 29:10-11:

- chiefs, BDB 910

- tribal members, BDB 986

- tribal elders, BDB 278

- tribal officers, BDB 1009, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- all the men of Israel, BDB 481, 35, 975 (same as #2)

- children, BDB 381

- wives, BDB 61

- resident aliens, BDB 158

- servants, described in their servant tasks

All these different groups are called upon to attest to their commitment to the covenant (cf. Deut. 29:14-15). This
was a formal covenant renewal ceremony!

The number of groups mentioned varies from translation to translation. Some translations (REB) assume
that #1 and #2 should be combined (e.g. KJV, "your captains of your tribes," JPSOA, "your tribal leaders"). The ASV, NASB,
NIV all have #1-4.

29:12-13 This is a covenant renewal text. Notice how "the covenant" (BDB 136) and "the oath" (BDB 46) are
parallel (i.e. Gen. 26:28). YHWH's regulations are linked to His promises!

YHWH wants to culminate the promises made to the Patriarchs in Genesis by establishing a people
(cf. Deut. 28:9), a people who reflect His character!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

29:12

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, LXX, JPSOA
"that you may enter

into the covenant"

NJB
"and you are about

to pass into the

covenant

Peshitta
"that you may not

transgress the

covenant"

The VERBAL (BDB 716, KB 778, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) literally
means "pass over." It is used only in the sense of entering into a covenant here. It is possibly connected to the idea of "cutting"
a covenant by passing between the parts of the sacrificial animal as in Gen. 15:17-18. The inference is that the fate of the animal
will pass on to the one making the covenant if they disobey the stipulations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 29:14-21

14"Now not with you alone am I making this covenant and this oath, 15but both with
those who stand here with us today in the presence of the Lord our God and with those who are not with us here today 16(for you
know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we came through the midst of the nations through which you passed; 17moreover, you have seen their
abominations and their idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold, which they had with them); 18so that there will not be among you a man or woman,
or family or tribe, whose heart turns away today from the Lord our God, to go and serve the gods of those nations; that there will not be among
you a root bearing poisonous fruit and wormwood. 19It shall be when he hears the words of this curse, that he will boast, saying, 'I have peace though I walk in
the stubbornness of my heart in order to destroy the watered land with the dry.' 20The Lord shall never be willing to forgive
him, but rather the anger of the Lord and His jealousy will burn against that man, and every curse which is written in this book will rest on him, and
the Lord will blot out his name from under heaven. 21Then the Lord will single him out for adversity
from all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant which are written in this book of the law."

29:15 "and with those who are not with us here today" This refers to future generations (cf. Deut. 29:22,29; 5:3-5; 12:25,28).

29:16-17 These verses form a summary parenthesis about the pagan nations Israel encountered in its pilgrimage to the Promised Land.

▣ "their abominations" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION

▣ "their idols" See SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL FAITH IS CORPORATE

29:20 "The Lord shall never be willing to forgive him" This hyperbole must be
seen against the background of YHWH's willingness to forgive and accept any repentant believer (i.e. Deut. 30:1-10).

Some Bible teachers link this verse with Ps. 103:9 and assert that there is a limit or threshold to YHWH's grace.
I do not accept this. Psalm 103:9 in context (i.e. Deut. 29:8-14) shows He will forgive! The problem is not God's forgiveness, but fallen,
rebellious mankind's continual sin! The relationship is broken from mankind's side and it remains broken from mankind's side. Unbelief
and rebellion issue in destruction, both temporally and eternally!

29:22-23 YHWH's blessing, which was meant to attract those who did not know Him, will be turned into a
mocking questioning by foreigners:

- plagues of the land, Deut. 29:22

- diseases, Deut. 29:22

- land is brimstone, Deut. 29:23

- land is salt, Deut. 29:23

- land is a burning waste, Deut. 29:23

- land is sown, and no germination, Deut. 29:23

- land is unproductive, Deut. 29:23

- land has no grass, Deut. 29:23

- land like the cities of the Plain (cf. Gen. 19:24)

All of these YHWH sent (cf. Deut. 29:22-28).

29:22 "Now the generation to come. . .will say" This literary form (i.e. children asking questions) is seen
earlier in Deut. 6:20, which reflects Exod. 13:8,14; 10:2; 12:26,27. Deuteronomy often speaks of teaching the children
(e.g. Deut. 4:10; 6:7).

29:23 "All its land is brimstone and salt" The land will be as the southern Dead Sea area, which was the site of
Sodom and Gomorrah (cf. Gen. 19:24-26).

29:24 "And all nations will say" Israel was a sign to all nations concerning YHWH (i.e. Ezek. 36:22-36). It was meant
to be a blessing sign but even if judgment, still a sign!

29:25 "Because they forsook the covenant" This was and is the basic reason for the divine curses
(cf. 2 Kgs. 17:9-23; 2 Chr. 36:13-21).

29:26 "gods. . .gods" Literally this is Elohim. This term is PLURAL. It usually is translated
"God" (i.e. when combined with a SINGULAR VERB). It can also refer to angelic beings and judges.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why did God have the covenant renewed so often (Deut. 29:1)?

- Why did God blind the eyes of the Jews to His purposes (Deut. 29:4-6)?

- Does God ever become unwilling to forgive man (Deut. 29:20)?

- Why does the land suffer for man's sins (Deut. 29:27)?

- What is Deut. 29:29 referring to?
